explanations.Q7Z-4103455-3: This entry (Q7Z-4103455-3) has $1,520 in principal plus $88.11 interest stuck on an AD/CVD suspension. File the refund request in CAPE now so the IEEPA duties come off, but the actual money won’t arrive until Commerce lifts the suspension. There’s no deadline shown, so act promptly to get in line. The uncertain part is when Commerce will lift the suspension — that timing controls when you’re paid.
explanations.Q7Z-4103309-2: This entry requires a Post Summary Correction (PSC) to be filed before you can submit a CAPE claim for the IEEPA refund. You must file the PSC first — it cannot itself claim the refund — and only after it’s accepted can you proceed with the CAPE filing. No deadline or liquidation date is provided, so the timing is uncertain; act promptly to avoid missing any future cutoff. The guidance carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning it’s probable but not definitive, so verify with your broker or CBP if anything seems unclear.
explanations.Q7Z-4101559-4: This entry was liquidated 81–180 days ago, so the CAPE refund route is closed for now. You must file a protest in ACE by **2026-10-27 (in 2 days)** to keep your rights alive, and you should also ask counsel whether a CIT case makes sense for the $1,567.50 principal plus $125.01 interest. The “P” confidence tag means the rule is probable but not certain, and the fentanyl/reciprocal-baseline programs may affect eligibility in ways the engine doesn’t quantify. No other refund path is available today without a protest or court action.
explanations.K4M-9231751-6: This entry shows a $1,122.58 refund (principal plus interest) that belongs to the importer of record — not you — so you cannot claim it directly. The liquidation date (estimated June 6, 2026) must be confirmed in ACE, and you have until December 3, 2026 (39 days) to file a protest under 19 U.S.C. 1514 to preserve any rights. Because the CAPE path is closed, your only near-term options are filing that protest or consulting counsel about a Court of International Trade case. Uncertainty: the exact liquidation date and whether the actual importer of record has already acted.
explanations.Q7Z-4102801-9: This entry contains only a $530 Section 122 surcharge, which is not eligible for refund through the CAPE/IEEPA process. To preserve any chance of recovery, you (or your broker) must file a protest under 19 U.S.C. § 1514(c)(3) within 180 days of the entry’s liquidation date. Because the liquidation date isn’t provided, the exact protest deadline is unknown — ask your broker or counsel to confirm it immediately. Until that date is confirmed, the ability to act in time remains uncertain.
explanations.Q7Z-4103107-0:
Your entry (Q7Z-4103107-0) has an open protest, and CAPE will reject any protested entry. If the protest covers **only** the IEEPA claim and today falls within 80 days of the 2026‑06‑25 liquidation (i.e., on or after 2026‑04‑06), you should withdraw the protest and file a CAPE claim in ACE; otherwise, keep the protest in place.  
**What to do now:** Ask your licensed broker to confirm the protest’s scope and whether the current date is inside that 80‑day window, then act accordingly.  
**Uncertainties:** The protest’s exact subject matter, today’s date relative to the 80‑day cutoff, and the rule’s confidence level (tagged “probable”) all affect the correct next step.
explanations.Q7Z-4103424-9: Your warehouse entry (type 21/22) can no longer be processed in CAPE as of July 7, 2026, so the $1,640 principal plus $69.31 interest will not refund through this entry. You must file withdrawal entries (types 31/32/34/38) instead to recover the duties. No deadline is shown in the data, so confirm the filing window with your broker or ACE account. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning the guidance may still be subject to change.
explanations.Q7Z-4101104-9: This entry was liquidated on August 9, 2026, making it eligible for a tariff refund under the CAPE program, but CBP must accept the filing within 80 days of liquidation. You have only 3 days left (until October 28, 2026) to file the refund claim in ACE through your broker or directly. The refund would cover $1,810 principal plus $115.34 interest, though the applicability of the “India (Russian oil)” and “Reciprocal” programs is not guaranteed. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning the interpretation is plausible but not certain; confirm with your broker before filing.
